1: # Proposed windows-reservation02 qualification
2: 
3: Status: prepared, not executed or admitted. Root must review the exact source,
4: tests, launcher and PINS before one first run. No native launch is included.

7: qualify_windows_reservations.py, and explicit IG_FORBIDDEN_LIVE set before child
8: startup. run_preflight01.ps1 requires a fresh windows-reservation02 output,
9: approved root admission for that exact label and PINS digest, and exactly 28
10: flat input bindings. Copy and verify those inputs and all three control records
11: before invoking the child. Scrub provider credentials and Python/proxy variables.
12: No account, downloaded package, interpreter site processing or model is used.
13: 
14: The runner derives from the qualified 42-case reservation runner preserved in
15: origins. It adds only contextlib/hmac/re/stat stdlib preloads for the fixed source
16: imports and explicitly loads 17 reviewed local modules from bounded captured
17: bytes. It executes their definitions under the existing closed content/import,
18: 12 metadata traps and 25 baseline-winreg callable traps. No ctypes/native library
19: or process/pipe service is installed. The current C314 built-in winreg startup
20: expectation is inherited from the preserved successful reservation42 and prior
21: lcs02 evidence; this proposal runs no new startup probe.
22: 
23: Execute the unchanged 42 original case bodies, with only the fixed fake kernel's
24: new finish_start method to match the split interface, followed by 23 new cases.
25: The exact 65 ordered case IDs are in EXPECTED-CASES.json. Nested subtests are
26: recorded within their parent cases and are not extra test counts. The new module
27: imports the original test module instead of exposing its TestCase class directly,
28: avoiding accidental duplicate discovery.
29: 
30: The new controls exercise the actual Windows journal/gate source against fixed
31: in-memory FFI/handle/disk services, including second-registry exclusion, partial
32: writes, ancestor/result/identity failures, cached confirmation poisoning, close
33: failure and the closed real entry. They exercise the actual durable split's
34: finish ordering, failure stop and late publication refusal. The actual migrated
35: adapter and its no-worker flow are called against fake services; original read-set
36: retirement source runs with an inert handle-close port. Checks cover ensure_assets,
37: initial admission failure, fresh generation on the same registry, retained gate
38: on cleanup failure, invalid no-worker states, exact durable-factory acceptance
39: and old-factory refusal. Fake service behavior does not qualify Windows semantics.
40: 
41: The runner compares exact ordered membership and all ten final guard conditions,
42: including unchanged refusal entrypoints, absent resolver approval and restored
43: adapter service globals. It records every actual case outcome, nested failure,
44: guard result, source digest and elapsed time. Content reads remain closed after
45: source capture. The 256-KiB receipt cap remains unchanged. These controls constrain
46: content/import/metadata and reviewed API behavior; they are not an OS sandbox.
47: 
48: The launcher sets PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=false immediately before
49: the child, captures global:LASTEXITCODE without a local reset, and writes the native
50: exit receipt before postchecks. It then verifies all original/copied inputs and
51: controls, empty stderr, exact 65 membership, all guard fields and true exits.
52: Preserve the actual outer tool object separately. Any failure stays failed; stop
53: and write a repair brief before any new label. No retry is authorized here.
54: 
55: This proposed observation cannot establish actual cross-process Windows locks,
56: FlushFileBuffers behavior, native ABI/cancellation, startup/IPC liveness, restart
57: reconciliation, real namespace authority, installed runtime or model readiness.
58: Those remain separate concrete generated-native protocols after source review.
